licence: official public guidance and technical specification
core_claims: National Polygon boundaries are indicative rather than exact legal extents
overlaps gaps slivers and underlaps exist in the dataset
technical overlaps may arise from mapping inconsistency without a real title conflict
actual overlaps can represent genuinely overlapping registered extents
minor overlaps below 0.5 square metres are not referred for remedial action
overlap can be acceptable for strata tenure or class-of-title reasons
an index polygon can be the same size larger or smaller than the title-plan extent
historic index polygons were manually captured on county sheets grid sheets and parcel books
the 2004 conversion project vectorised about 19 million paper polygons
converted polygons were mapped against OS Land-Line
temporary capture practice used pictorial completion and title plans were seldom used for validation
the Positional Accuracy Improvement programme ran from 2005 to 2008
the Quality Improvement Flowline processed almost 14 million polygons around 2009
OS MasterMap replaced Land-Line in later reconciliation work
title plans and index polygons are not routinely updated
customer queries can trigger polygon maintenance
an incorrect adjoining registration noticed during another application can trigger maintenance
a noticed polygon error can trigger maintenance
sale of part can require removal of land from a title and polygon
daily created updated and deleted polygons are uploaded overnight to publication
publication validation checks zero coordinates zero areas and duplicate coordinate points
self-intersections may be cleaned and areas below 0.1 square metres removed from publication
change-only delivery contains only the latest version
previous polygon versions are not retained in the change-only delivery
